events.title: 70 Years of RSP: Where Design Meets Humanity
events.overview: Discover 70 years of Singapore architecture through RSP’s work, including 15 models of familiar projects such as Henderson Waves, Jewel Changi Airport and the Indoor Stadium, plus original drawings and design records.
events.why: A free exhibition for anyone curious about how well-known Singapore buildings and public spaces were designed.
events.venue: The URA Centre · Level 1 Atrium, 45 Maxwell Road

events.title: Bit Bit Forest Mid-Autumn Light Up!
events.overview: Giant illuminated Bit Bit Forest bunny inflatables by Hong Kong-based Kau’s Diary transform the Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre Roof Garden and Concourse for Mid-Autumn.
events.why: A free, easy-going evening stop for colourful photos and a festive atmosphere, especially if you are already visiting the cultural centre.
events.venue: Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre · Roof Garden

events.title: Crossing Borders 2026
events.overview: A month of free music and cultural performances from the Middle East, Asia, Europe and the Americas. The 26–27 September weekend includes Okinawan music, Korean dance, Latin American performances and Afro-Brazilian percussion.
events.why: Good for a flexible weekend visit because you can choose from several free performances rather than committing to one long ticketed show.

events.title: Into the Ocean: Journey Beneath
events.overview: A world-premiere ArtScience Museum exhibition with OceanX that takes visitors from sunlit surface waters into the deep ocean through footage, specimens, research and immersive displays.
events.why: A strong indoor choice if you enjoy nature documentaries, marine life, science and immersive museum experiences.

events.title: Lai Foong Moi: Crossings
events.overview: See 1960s Singapore and Malaya through the paintings of Lai Foong Moi, with portraits, landscapes and everyday scenes exploring identity, social change and belonging.
events.why: A quieter cultural outing for visitors interested in Singapore and Malayan social history seen through art.
events.venue: National Gallery Singapore · City Hall Wing, Level 2
events.senior: Local: Free · overseas senior 60+: $5 off standard
events.child: Local: Free · age 7–12 overseas: $5 off; 6 & under free

events.title: Mid-Autumn Festival 2026
events.overview: Gardens by the Bay lights up with lantern displays across Golden Garden, Dragonfly Lake, Supertree Grove and other areas, plus a marketplace, carnival activities and selected craft programmes.
events.why: This is the final weekend, making it a timely choice for an evening outing with lanterns, food stalls and festive performances.
events.venue: Gardens by the Bay · Multiple outdoor locations

events.title: Singapore TV: From Local to Global
events.overview: A nostalgic journey through Singapore Chinese television dramas from the 1960s to today. Five themed zones feature original costumes, artefacts, photographs, magazines, recreated sets, multimedia and interactive experiences.
events.why: A strong pick if you remember local Chinese dramas from the 1970s–1990s and want to revisit familiar programmes, stars, costumes and TV memories.
events.venue: Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre · Creative Box, Level 6

events.title: Small Screen, Big Stories: Telemovies of the 1990s
events.overview: Revisit classic made-for-TV movies that were a familiar Saturday-night feature in Singapore from 1994 to 1997. The 26 September screenings are When a Child Is Born and The Matchmaker’s Match.
events.why: Ideal as a companion outing to the Singapore TV exhibition if you enjoy 1990s local television nostalgia.
events.venue: Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre · Recital Studio, Level 6

events.title: Tails from the Coasts: Nature Stories of Singapore
events.overview: An exhibition at the National Museum exploring nature stories connected with Singapore’s coasts, adding an environmental perspective to the museum’s Singapore-focused displays.
events.why: A free indoor option for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents that combines nature, local stories and museum time.

events.title: The Albatross File: Singapore’s Independence Declassified
events.overview: Go behind the scenes of Singapore’s merger and separation from Malaysia using newly declassified documents, oral-history accounts and material tracing the crucial years from 1963 to 1965.
events.why: A substantial free history exhibition for visitors who want a deeper understanding of how independent Singapore came about.
